Growing later is a nice thought, friend, but James doesn't bring it up. He looks at the faith that's sitting there right now and asks, "Can such faith save him?" It's like asking about the dough already on the tray, not the batch I'm hoping for next week. Same person, same claim, and James wants to know about that.

Right on target, baker. James says this brother or sister is "without clothes and daily food." Those are the basics, the stuff you need every single day. Notice he calls them a brother or sister, so this is a fellow believer, someone close.

A home and steady work are real needs, friend, but they aren't in James's picture. He says the brother or sister is without clothes and daily food. I think that's the kind of need you can see the moment you look at someone. James keeps it that simple.

Hidden sounds gentle, friend, like a faith tucked in the back of a shelf waiting to come out. But James doesn't say hidden. He says faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead. Hidden things are still there, and James picks a much stronger word.

explanations.answer: He'll show his faith by his deeds
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. James says, "Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds." He doesn't argue about it. He says you can see it. I think he's saying real faith has something you can point to.

That one's a fair guess, but James doesn't crown deeds either, friend. He says, "Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds." His deeds are how he shows his faith. He's not trading one in for the other.

explanations.answer: Welcomed the spies and sent them off another way
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. James says she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route. Joshua 2:4 says she took the two men and hid them. That's her action, and it's the one James points to.

explanations.answer: Turned the spies over to the king
explanations.explanation: That's not what James says, friend. He says she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route. The king of Jericho sent word asking for them (Joshua 2:3), but Joshua 2:4 says she had taken the two men and hidden them. So she was on the opposite side of that request.

explanations.answer: Kept the spies out of her house
explanations.explanation: Nope, the door was open, friend. Joshua 2:1 says the spies went to the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there. James says she welcomed them, then sent them off on another route. A closed door would have made a very short story.
